title: Canadian Effective Exchange Rates
summary: This Bank of Canada page is a methodology reference document explaining the Canadian Effective Exchange Rate (CEER) index, which replaced the CERI in January 2018. It describes how the index is constructed using 17 currencies weighted by trade patterns (imports, exports, and third-market competition), with separate sub-indices for major currencies and other important trading partners. Data is available for download in XML, JSON, and CSV formats. No current exchange rate values or market catalyst content is provided.
key_points: CEER is a weighted average of bilateral exchange rates against 17 trading partner currencies, covering over 93% of Canadian non-oil exports and 91% of non-oil imports
The index includes two sub-indices: major currencies (USD, EUR, JPY, GBP, CHF, AUD, SEK) and OITP (10 currencies including CNY, MXN, KRW, BRL, INR)
Energy trade is excluded from weight calculations to maintain consistency with international standards and minimize volatility from oil price swings
Weights are calculated as equal halves of import share and a combination of export share plus third-market competition
The page is a static methodology reference page with no publication date, no current data values, and no market catalyst content
Data is available for download in XML, JSON, and CSV formats for nominal (daily/monthly) and real (monthly) indices

macro_context: The CEER index tracks the Canadian dollar against 17 trading partner currencies using multilateral trade weights. The major currencies sub-index (USD, EUR, JPY, GBP, CHF, AUD, SEK) captures financial pressure dynamics, while the OITP sub-index captures competitiveness effects. Energy trade is excluded from weights per international standards.
